caption:
Nobody buys from a Reel. They buy after the fourth story where you were just a person.

A Reel's job is to get a stranger to decide you might be worth following. That's a two-second judgement about competence.

Buying is a different judgement entirely. It takes repetition, a face, small unglamorous details, and the feeling that there's someone on the other end who will answer. Stories are the only surface built for that — they go to people who already chose you, and they rank on whether you tap in and reply.

This is why "my Reels go viral but nothing sells" is so common. Those are two separate machines and most people only built one.

Practical version: use Reels to be found, Stories to be trusted, and DMs to close. If you have no story habit, you have a top of funnel and nothing under it.

Story ads average an 82% completion rate across industries. People do watch to the end. Give them something to watch.
